{"slug": "kodely-vs-v0", "title": "Kodely vs v0: Which AI Builder Should You Use? (2026)", "metaTitle": "Kodely vs v0: Which AI Builder Should You Use? (2026)", "metaDescription": "An honest, side-by-side comparison of Kodely and v0 - pricing, code access, hosting, security and who each is best for.", "targetKeyword": "kodely vs v0", "category": "Comparisons", "bodyHtml": "

Kodely and v0 both turn a text prompt into working React code, but they are built for different people. v0, from Vercel, is a UI-generation tool for developers who already work in React and want to scaffold components fast. Kodely is a chat-to-live-site builder aimed at people who do not want to touch code at all. Here is an honest breakdown of where each one actually wins.

TL;DR verdict

CategoryKodelyv0
Best forNon-developers who want a live site fastDevelopers scaffolding UI inside an existing workflow
OutputFull Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 appReact components, often shadcn/Tailwind based
Going liveOne-click publish to a free <name>.kodely.site URLDeploy separately via Vercel
Code accessView and copy source in-app, no export yetCopy or export code, designed to plug into your repo
BackendFrontend only, no backend/auth/database generationFrontend focused, backend wired up manually by the developer
PricingMetered credits, failed builds are freeTied to Vercel plans and usage

Pricing and the credit model

Kodely runs on a straightforward metered-credit system. New accounts get 750 free credits with no credit card required. A first build typically costs 100 to 150 credits, and a follow-up change usually costs about the same. If a generation fails to compile, Kodely runs one automatic repair attempt and never charges you for the failure - you only pay for a build that actually works. When you need more credits, top-ups are $9 for 500 credits, $40 for 2,500 credits (the most popular option), or $90 for 6,000 credits, and credits never expire.

v0 is built into Vercel's own pricing structure, with a free tier for limited generations and paid usage tied to Vercel's plans. That makes it convenient if you already pay for Vercel, but the cost model is bundled with hosting and platform usage rather than a flat, standalone credit price. Because Vercel's plans change over time, check v0.dev directly for current numbers - the honest comparison here is philosophy, not exact figures: Kodely's pricing is isolated and predictable per generation, v0's is part of a broader platform bill.

Do you own the code?

Neither tool hands you a locked black box, but access works differently. In v0, code is the product - you are meant to copy generated components straight into your own codebase and keep building there. In Kodely, every project is a real app made of real .tsx component files, and you can view and copy that source directly in the editor. What Kodely does not have yet is a zip or full-project export - there is no download button for the whole codebase. If your workflow depends on pulling a project out and running it in your own repo today, that is a real limitation worth knowing before you start.

Hosting and going live

This is where the two tools diverge most. v0 generates components; putting them in front of real users means deploying, which usually means a Vercel account, a project setup, and Next.js knowledge if you want the full integration. That is a strength if you are already living in that ecosystem, and friction if you are not.

Kodely skips that step entirely. Publish is one click inside the same chat interface you used to build the app, and it puts the site live on a free .kodely.site subdomain with no separate hosting account, no deploy configuration, and no extra cost. The tradeoff is that Kodely does not yet support custom domains - you get a kodely.site address, not yourdomain.com.

Backend depth

Be clear-eyed here: neither tool ships a backend for you out of the box in the way a full-stack platform might imply. Kodely generates a real frontend app only - no database, no authentication, and no payments generation. v0 is similarly frontend-oriented at its core, though because it lives inside the Vercel/Next.js ecosystem, developers who know what they are doing can wire it up to serverless functions, databases, and auth themselves. If you need real backend logic today, you will be adding it by hand either way - v0 just gives an experienced developer a more familiar set of levers to do that with.

Security

Kodely scans every publish for accidentally-leaked secrets and API keys before the site goes live, catching a common mistake where a generated app ends up shipping a key in client-side code. This runs automatically on every publish, not as an opt-in setting. v0 does not do this kind of automated pre-deploy scan itself - since deployment happens through your own Vercel project, secret management is on you, same as any other codebase you deploy manually.

Who each one is actually best for

Pick v0 if you already write React, live in the Vercel/Next.js ecosystem, and want an AI assistant to scaffold components you will then wire up yourself. It gives you more control over the generated code and fits naturally into an existing engineering workflow.

Pick Kodely if you do not know React and just want to describe a site and have it exist - live, on a real URL, without opening a terminal. The honest gap is real: no custom domains, no code export, and no backend generation. The honest edge is also real: no separate deploy step, transparent per-build pricing where failures cost nothing, and a product built for people who have never written a line of code.

FAQ

Can I move a Kodely project into my own codebase?

You can view and copy the generated component files from inside Kodely today. There is no one-click zip export yet, so migrating a full project out currently means copying files manually.

Does v0 host my site for me?

Not by itself. v0 generates the code; you deploy it, typically through Vercel, which is a separate step with its own account and setup.

Which one is cheaper?

It depends on usage, but Kodely's pricing is simpler to reason about: a flat credit cost per generation, free retries on failed builds, and credits that never expire. v0's cost is tied into whatever Vercel plan you are on.

Do I need to know how to code to use Kodely?

No. You describe what you want in plain English and Kodely builds and publishes it. Further changes work the same way - describe them in chat.

Ready to see it for yourself? Start building free on Kodely and publish your first live site in minutes.
